faq.q: Who is exempt from paying advance tax?
faq.a: Resident senior citizens (aged 60 years or above) who do not have income from business or profession are exempt. Also, if your estimated tax liability after TDS is less than ₹10,000, you don't need to pay advance tax.

faq.q: What happens if I miss the September 15th deadline?
faq.a: If you miss the September 15th deadline or pay less than 45% of your total estimated tax by then, you may be charged interest under Section 234C of the Income Tax Act for deferment of advance tax.

faq.q: How do I calculate my advance tax?
faq.a: You need to estimate your total income for the financial year, calculate the tax on it, and then subtract any TDS/TCS. The remaining amount, if ₹10,000 or more, is your advance tax liability, which you then divide into installments.

faq.q: Can I revise my advance tax estimate during the year?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. If your income situation changes (e.g., unexpected capital gains, new income source, or higher/lower business profits), you should re-estimate your tax liability and adjust your subsequent advance tax installments accordingly. This helps avoid underpayment penalties.

faq.q: What is the Assessment Year (AY) for FY 2026-27?
faq.a: The Assessment Year (AY) for the Financial Year (FY) 2026-27 will be AY 2027-28. When paying advance tax online, ensure you select the correct Assessment Year.
